exposure: SARS-CoV-2 infection in unvaccinated participants during pregnancy
SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in the absence of infection during pregnancy
outcome: placental transfer of antibodies to the fetus
cohort: Pregnant patients (n = 165) enrolled at Oregon Health & Science University, categorized into three groups based on their SARS-CoV-2 infection and vaccination status.
finding: Breakthrough SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy induces a higher maternal RBD-specific IgG response and facilitates greater transplacental transfer of antibodies to the neonate compared to infection or vaccination alone, reflecting an antibody priming effect from prior vaccination.
